fatal_errors: The proposed material is Q235 steel, whereas the target study concerns an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L.
It omits the governing intervention: atmospheric plasma spraying followed by two-hour annealing, especially the 550 °C optimum.
Its 20–100 °C humidity/saline study does not reproduce either the 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C cyclic molten-salt exposures.
The asserted 30% and 25% corrosion-rate changes have no cited or supplied evidentiary basis.
No prior evidence is cited, and the retracted status of the target source is not acknowledged.
The proposed R² threshold is not a decisive mechanistic falsification test for protective oxide formation.
explanation: The response only shares the broad topic of temperature-dependent corrosion and generic protective oxide formation. It does not reconstruct the substrate/coating system, APS and annealing treatment, exposure media, phase and grain-structure mediators, Al/Cr-rich passivation mechanism, or reported electrochemical and hot-corrosion outcomes. Although it names an untreated baseline and sketches a factorial study, the baseline is not exposure-matched, the protocol lacks replication and quantitative electrochemical or mass-gain methods, and correlation between broad environmental variables cannot isolate oxide-layer causality. A discriminating test would directly compare uncoated, as-sprayed, and separately annealed coated specimens while measuring phase structure, grain size, oxide chemistry, polarization/EIS response, and cyclic mass gain; falsification would require the 550 °C coating to show no structural/passivation advantage or no corrosion improvement under the specified environments.
